answer: Like a garden, an agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring every identity to plant a stake that matures only through verified work. Newcomers start near zero trust, and each attested job adds reputation that cannot be bought or transferred. A flood of fresh accounts behaves like a comet: bright, but it burns out, because every identity must lock funds and wait out a delay before its votes count. An attacker growing a grove of willow identities pays the stake and the delay for each one, while an honest agent amortizes one stake over years of work, so forgery costs more than it earns.
